fidelity_limits: Simulation only; no hardware, realtime or continuous-time guarantee follows.
Weights are numerical recipe parameters on a frozen controller implementation.
The holding-speed acceptance threshold is inferred from sparse samples, not certified.

plan.hypothesis: On the frozen compliant shortened structure, the holding-speed failures for holding>=0.06 at terminal weight 0.05 are caused by a terminal×holding weight interaction that is reproducible: re-executing the source (holding 0.09, terminal 0.05) reproduces its failing holding speed, and an intermediate terminal weight (holding 0.09, terminal 0.075) moves holding speed toward the passing (0.09, 0.10) result.
plan.rationale: Holding is fixed at the frozen source value 0.09 and only control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight is varied, isolating the terminal-weight lever that separated the recorded (0.09,0.05) fail from the (0.09,0.10) pass. Candidate 1 exactly repeats the source configuration as a deliberate replication to test run-to-run reproducibility (solver-plan selection); candidate 2 is a novel intermediate terminal weight to test whether the terminal rescue is graded or discrete. This references the actual first-batch feedback, stays within the frozen structure and controller, and spends the two remaining backend attempts on the cheapest decisive contrast.
plan.replication_reason: Candidate 1 re-executes the exact frozen source configuration (holding 0.09, terminal 0.05, compliant shortened structure) to test run-to-run reproducibility against a solver-plan-selection artifact; candidate 2 is a novel intermediate terminal weight, not a replication.
stopping_conditions: Both candidates complete with full profile and retained bound facts.
weakening_observations: A replicated (holding 0.09, terminal 0.05) that yields a passing holding speed (below the sampled fail band ~0.022) would indicate solver-plan selection dominates a deterministic weight effect.
A (holding 0.09, terminal 0.075) result that fails with a holding speed near the 0.05-terminal failures would show the terminal rescue is not a graded interaction but requires the full 0.10 value.
A (holding 0.09, terminal 0.075) result numerically equal (within 1e-09) to the (0.09, 0.10) pass would suggest a discrete switch rather than a smooth interaction.

interpretations.scope: controller.gvs_nmpc@7.0.0, frozen compliant shortened structure (near 0.16 m, far 0.11 m, section 0.95), sampled holding/terminal tip-speed weights
interpretations.statement: On the frozen compliant shortened structure at fixed terminal weight 0.05, holding-speed acceptance flips from pass at holding 0.05 (~0.0127 m/s) to fail at holding 0.06 (0.023994623331658485), while the same holding 0.09 passes at terminal 0.10 (0.010201160469407439), so a terminal×holding weight interaction plausibly governs acceptance rather than a fixed holding threshold.
interpretations.uncertainty: Only a small sampled set; no intermediate terminal weight between 0.05 and 0.10; solver-plan selection and structural sensitivity are not excluded.

interpretations.scope: frozen compliant shortened structure, joint-positive holding/terminal weight region
interpretations.statement: Run-to-run reproducibility of these holding outcomes is untested; the sharp, near-factor-2 jump between holding 0.05 and 0.06 is also compatible with a discrete solver-plan switch rather than a graded weight effect.
interpretations.uncertainty: No identical configuration has been executed twice in the campaign store, so repetition cannot yet be distinguished from a deterministic weight effect.

decision.reasoning: The current feedback is confined to the frozen compliant shortened structure (structure a6099...; near 0.16, far 0.11, section 0.95). At fixed terminal weight 0.05 the holding speed jumps from a pass at holding 0.05 (~0.0127 m/s, F513/F353 class) to a fail at holding 0.06 (0.023994623331658485, F437/F280) and stays failing for 0.075/0.09/0.10 holding (F375/F319 = 0.02260458517372844 for the source 0.09/0.05). Yet the SAME holding 0.09 passes once terminal weight is raised to 0.10 (0.010201160469407439, F258/F360, holding_speed_passed true F328). So the recorded pattern is compatibly explained by a terminal×holding weight interaction rather than a fixed holding threshold, while two named alternatives remain untested: solver-plan selection (no repeated execution of any identical configuration exists — the sharp near-factor-2 jump could be a discrete plan switch) and structural sensitivity (all samples share one structure identity). Budget allows exactly one more batch with at most two backend attempts. The cheapest discriminatory pair is (i) an explicit re-execution of the frozen source (holding 0.09, terminal 0.05) to test run-to-run reproducibility, and (ii) one novel intermediate terminal weight (holding 0.09, terminal 0.075) at fixed holding to test whether the terminal-weight rescue is graded or discrete. This keeps holding fixed, changes only the terminal weight, references the first-batch evidence directly, and does not attempt the structurally confounded route.
unresolved_uncertainties: Whether the holding-speed jump at terminal 0.05 is a smooth weight effect or a discrete solver-plan switch.
